prompt: Binary-search a case-insensitively sorted String array for a target, ignoring case. Complete the find method using Arrays.binarySearch with String.CASE_INSENSITIVE_ORDER, returning -1 when absent.
explanation: Arrays.binarySearch only works if the array is sorted by the SAME comparator you search with, so a case-insensitively sorted array must be searched with String.CASE_INSENSITIVE_ORDER. When the target is missing, binarySearch returns -(insertionPoint) - 1, a negative number that encodes where the value would belong; since this exercise only asks whether the value exists, any negative result is normalized to -1.
hints: Use the three-argument overload: Arrays.binarySearch(array, target, comparator).
String.CASE_INSENSITIVE_ORDER is a ready-made Comparator<String> constant on the String class.
binarySearch returns a negative insertion point for misses -- test the result with >= 0 and return -1 otherwise.
